learningObjective: Read a binary noisy channel's joint distribution to distinguish marginal uncertainty, remaining conditional uncertainty, and the mutual information removed by observing the output.
mediumRationale: Two semantic tables are the smallest medium that can align the binary channel's four joint outcomes with a before-after uncertainty budget. The shared 0.5 marginals remain visible while the diagonal concentration explains why observing Y still reduces uncertainty about X.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected because a flowchart can show X passing through noise to Y but cannot make the joint probabilities, unchanged marginals, or entropy subtraction directly inspectable.
mediumComparison.svg: Rejected because custom geometry adds no precision beyond real table cells and would make the probability data less accessible and selectable.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Selected because a joint-probability table and a compact entropy ledger preserve row and column semantics, exact arithmetic, natural reading order, and responsive stacking.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected because varying the crossover probability would add controls and mutable states when the article already provides changed-assumption practice; one deterministic 10% channel is enough to establish the decomposition.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected because textbook information diagrams and channel figures are unnecessary, and public access does not establish permission to reuse them. No external figure, layout, prose, or dataset is copied.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected because the equations state H(X), H(X|Y), and I(X;Y), but prose alone makes it hard to see how both marginals can remain one full bit while their dependence still removes 0.531 bits of uncertainty.

pages.insight: The parameter-learning slide connects maximum likelihood, cross-entropy, and KL divergence, but does not define entropy, conditional entropy, or mutual information.

The random-forest slide defines binary class entropy and says tree splits maximize entropy reduction, providing an application of information gain without deriving conditional entropy or mutual information.
The neighboring split-criterion slide names information gain for categorical targets but gives no weighted-child formula or worked split.
The preceding character-language-model slide supplies sequence-prediction context but does not discuss entropy or shared information.
The tokenization-and-perplexity slide relates perplexity to entropy and next-token uncertainty; it does not distinguish predictive cross-entropy from source entropy or explain mutual information.
The following representation-learning slide describes autoregressive and masked objectives but adds no information-theoretic decomposition.

The image-classification slide mentions differential entropy and dequantization, supplying a warning that continuous entropy differs from discrete entropy but no noisy-channel or mutual-information model.

deckReview.notes: All 214 pages of the local PDF were text-indexed page by page for entropy, conditional entropy, mutual information, information gain, KL divergence, and information theory. Every match was reviewed. The complete relevant neighborhoods on pages 16-18, 24-27, 97-99, and 146-148 were extracted; none defines mutual information or a binary noisy channel. No deck artwork, equations, code, wording, or layout is reused.

sources.title: Elements of Information Theory, Second Edition
sources.usage: Used as the authoritative textbook source for discrete entropy, conditional entropy, mutual information as uncertainty reduction and KL divergence, symmetry, bounds, and the binary symmetric channel calculation.
sources.license: The book is commercially published by Wiley, and no permissive license for reproducing its figures was identified. No figure, example layout, wording, or table is copied; the visual is an original calculation from the article's stated channel.

sources.title: A Mathematical Theory of Communication
sources.usage: Used as the primary historical source for entropy as uncertainty, equivocation as remaining uncertainty after a received signal, and noisy-channel information rate.
sources.license: The hosted scan retains its original Bell System Technical Journal publication context and provides no clear permissive reuse grant. No paper figure, prose, typography, or channel diagram is reproduced.

sourceReview.notes: The original worked example instantiates the article's fair binary symmetric channel at error probability 0.1. Independence of the fair input and noise gives joint probabilities P(0,0)=P(1,1)=0.45 and P(0,1)=P(1,0)=0.05, so both X and Y have 0.5/0.5 marginals and one bit of entropy. Given either Y value, X matches with probability 0.9 and flips with probability 0.1; therefore H2(X|Y)=h2(0.1)=0.469 bits and I2(X;Y)=1-0.469=0.531 bits. Values, wording, and layout are original.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, text-indexed all 214 deck pages and inspected every entropy-adjacent neighborhood, then checked Shannon's primary paper, Cover and Thomas's authoritative textbook, and official scikit-learn semantics. The selected visual targets the article's hardest mental model: unchanged marginal uncertainty can coexist with substantial shared information.

implementation.accessibility: The figure uses real tables with scoped row and column headers, explicit joint probabilities, written marginal totals, a textual entropy identity, and a caption that states the conclusion without color. The established two-panel primitive stacks below 640 CSS pixels for a 390-pixel viewport, theme tokens preserve dark-mode contrast, and shared print rules enforce a light high-contrast palette.
